name: Dare to Know: The Age of Reason
description: Philosophers, scientists, writers and rulers who tried to use reason against superstition and tyranny, from Newton's laws to the French Revolution.

checkpoints.name: The new science
checkpoints.note: The Royal Society promotes experiment, Newton's Principia explains the heavens, and Locke, Spinoza and Leibniz ask what we can know and how we should be governed.

checkpoints.name: Ideas on the move
checkpoints.note: Montesquieu studies how laws and governments work, Hume tests the limits of human reason, and Swift's Gulliver's Travels mocks the age with satire.

checkpoints.name: The encyclopedia years
checkpoints.note: Diderot edits the Encyclopédie, Voltaire fights intolerance, and the Lisbon earthquake tests faith in a perfect world, which Candide mocks. Rousseau's Social Contract challenges kings.

checkpoints.name: Reason and revolution
checkpoints.note: Smith explains the market, Kant asks what reason can know, and Franklin helps launch the American Revolution. In France the Declaration of the Rights of Man follows, and Wollstonecraft asks why women are left out.
